text:
alina: Anyone else seeing the infra CI failing on gha:gpu-nodepool-rotation this morning? terraform apply hangs in the matrix and helm apply times out repeatedly.
marc: yup, started ~06:12 UTC. failures across two zones. looks like the terraform apply step is stuck waiting on nodepool rollout.
joel: paste of the tail logs — kube provider aborting: 
```
2026-03-18T06:13:24Z [ERROR] provider.kubernetes: GET https://.../: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
2026-03-18T06:13:40Z [WARN] googleapi: Error 403: Quota exceeded for 'compute.googleapis.com'
```
priya: i saw a 403 on cache restore from actions/cache in a different job too. could be creds or a throttling blip. :thinking_face:
alina: the weird part is the matrix concurrency. we run 6 zones in parallel, each tries to provision GPUs and hits quota quickly. maybe throttle is killing kubeops.
infra-bot: workflow: gha/gpu-nodepool-rotation #3482 started by schedule, run_id=49921
marc: can we try lowering matrix parallelism to 2 for now? or add a concurrency group so we don't punch the cloud API so hard.
joel: quick workaround: add `concurrency: group: gpu-nodepool-rotation` to workflow and set `max-parallel: 2` in matrix (or use `strategy.max-parallel`). also add a retry wrapper around terraform apply step.
priya: i can repro cache 403: actions/cache returning 403 because the GCS token used by the runner expired mid-restore. logs show `storage: unauthorized` around same time as quota errors. suspicious.
alina: hmm creds rotation happened last night (kms key rolled). could be related. but the TLS handshake timeouts also point to busy control plane or node limits.
marc: another idea: switch the job to use a dedicated ephemeral runner in us-west1 for the rotation job until quotas calm down — that will serialize operations.
joel: small PR to test: change workflow to `max-parallel: 2`, increase `timeout-minutes` to 60 for helm/terraform steps, and add a pre-step to validate GCP service account token:
```
- name: Validate GCP token
  run: gcloud auth print-access-token --account=$GCP_SA || exit 1
```
priya: i'll own the cache/credentials angle. will check key rotation audit and see if the service account was missing iam.storage.objectViewer on the bucket.
alina: i'll open an incident ticket (INC-472) and apply the PR to reduce parallelism. can someone watch the runs?
devops-oncall: on it, watching the first reduced-matrix run now. will ping if it still hits the quota.
joel: if the reduced concurrency run still fails, we should add a 10s jittered sleep between zone provisions in terraform using `null_resource` local-exec as temporary throttle. ugly but effective.
marc: noted — also let's add better retry on helm `helm upgrade --install` (3 retries with backoff). shards of previous runs show helm times out after 120s.
priya: filed PR for credential fix and updated cache key in actions/cache to include runner-id to avoid reuse: PR #3899.
alina: thanks. applying the concurrency PR now. will update INC-472 with links to runs. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: run update: workflow gha/gpu-nodepool-rotation run_id=49922 status=queued
devops-oncall: queued -> in_progress. first run starting with max-parallel=2.
marc: watching cloud console — quota spikes still present but less severe. if green, we can keep reduced parallelism and schedule a dedicated quota bump request.
alina: plan: short-term reduce parallelism + retries, medium-term request quota increases and investigate key rotation impact. assigning follow-ups: priya -> creds/cache, joel -> workflow retries, marc -> quota request.
priya: i'll report back in 30m.
devops-oncall: run complete: success. terraform apply and helm apply completed for both zones.
alina: awesome. leaving INC-472 open until we confirm root cause. thanks all. :tada:
